market_mood: US stocks stabilized Friday after a post-election rally turned into an AI-trade meltdown, with a hot jobs report and a hawkish Fed keeping rate-hike risk alive.

themes.title: Midterm shock triggers AI/data-center rout
themes.what_happened: After Democrats won both chambers, AI-linked stocks sold off. On Nov 5 the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4%, the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, and all eleven S&P sectors lost ground. Nvidia fell 9.26% and lost about $450B in market value. Stocks stabilized Friday, with the S&P up about 1% and the Nasdaq up 1.9% in morning trade.
themes.why_it_matters: The election rout hit an AI trade already pressured by high interest rates, heavy capital spending and questions about returns, so investors are repricing how fast data centers get built.

our_exposure.why: Fell 9.26% to $181.60 on Nov 5. Data-center restriction fears hit GPU demand outlook.
Data-center power/cooling peers fell up to 20%+ Wednesday; VRT's own move not confirmed.
Power supplier to data centers. Slower buildout is a risk; its move not confirmed.
Hyperscaler earnings dented AI-spending enthusiasm; capex cuts would hurt suppliers but help AMZN's free cash flow.
Seen as relative winner; Polymarket now favors Apple over Nvidia as largest company.

themes.next: Nvidia reports after the close on Nov 17; one analyst said it must show revenue at or above its $108B guidance. Also watch for data-center moratorium proposals from the new Congress and state governments.

themes.title: Hot jobs report and hawkish Fed keep rate hikes in play
themes.what_happened: October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment ticked down to 4.1%. Yields rose: the 10-year was at 4.868% and the 2-year at 4.524%. The Fed held rates on Oct 28 with two dissents (Cook and Hammack) favoring a quarter-point hike. On Oct 28, a Dec 9 hike was priced at 85.7%, and the jobs report raised the odds further.
themes.why_it_matters: Inflation is running near 3.5% against the 2% target, and 10-year yields near 5% pressure long-duration equities and valuations.

our_exposure.why: High-beta retail broker; tighter financial conditions hit risk appetite and trading activity.
Long-duration growth multiple (about 44x trailing P/E) is sensitive to higher yields.
Higher rates help net interest income; a steeper curve and credit stress cut the other way.
Higher rates help net interest income; a steeper curve and credit stress cut the other way.
Strong jobs support spending volumes; higher yields compress multiples.
Strong jobs support spending volumes; higher yields compress multiples.

themes.next: The next FOMC meeting is Dec. 9. Watch the next inflation print and the 10-year yield around the 5% level.

themes.title: Oil slides on Iran-deal hopes, but tanker attacks keep it volatile
themes.what_happened: WTI fell 8.3% to $88.12 on Nov 4, oil's biggest daily decline since April. On Nov 5 Brent rose 3.8% to $98.29 and WTI rose 2.7% to $90.52. Brent is on track for a 12% weekly drop. Fresh tanker attacks in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz renewed supply worries.
themes.why_it_matters: The war pushed gasoline and diesel prices sharply higher, making stubborn inflation worse, so lower oil eases pressure on both the consumer and the Fed.

our_exposure.why: Lower oil cuts resin, freight and fuel costs, and supports consumer demand.
Lower fuel and logistics costs; consumer spending relief.
Lower gasoline prices free up consumer spending but trim fuel-driven transaction value.
Lower gasoline prices free up consumer spending but trim fuel-driven transaction value.

themes.next: Eurasia Group says escalation could push Brent to $110–$125. Watch Trump's decision on strikes versus a deal, and the Qatar-mediated talks.

themes.title: Lilly's blowout Q3 and guidance raise cushions the book, then it slips with the market
themes.what_happened: Q3 revenue jumped 39% to $24.4B, and Lilly raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91–92B from $85–87B. The stock rose 10% from Oct 28 to Nov 4 while the Nasdaq 100 fell 4.6%. It then closed down 3.76% at $1,364.73 on Nov 5.
themes.why_it_matters: LLY is our largest position at 17%. Its earnings-driven strength offset some of the tech damage, but it is not immune to broad risk-off selling.

our_exposure.why: Strong fundamentals and guidance, but fell 3.76% Nov 5 in the broad selloff.
Healthcare defensive; no company-specific news found, so this is a sector inference.

themes.next: LLY's ex-dividend date is Nov 13. Watch for any U.S. drug-pricing moves from the new Congress, which I did not find confirmed.
